The residue — Trapped melt · rack —

Set the history, then pour. Six phases crystallize in strict order of their liquidus temperature — each notch on the brass rail ignites as the falling temperature reaches it — and every crystal that forms settles, packing bands onto the chamber floor while the shrinking melt above walks from ember through straw to a strange violet-white. When the body stills, drag the brass drill down through the pile (or press Drive the drill, or focus the stage and use ↓ / Enter). It lifts a slender core and racks it: a mineral ladder up its length and a violet enrichment stripe beside it. Now throw the floor lever to STILL — the crystals never leave the liquid — and pull again. That core comes up blank, both readouts dead. Stand the two side by side; that pair is the whole point.

What this is honest about. The ladder, the numbers on the tags and the colours up the core are this model's own ordering — a clean laboratory of one idea (crystals form in liquidus order; removing them changes the liquid that is left). It is not a reading of any particular intrusion, and no real body is this tidy: nature reheats, mixes, assimilates its walls and lets crystals re-dissolve. What is exact here is the internal law — order, mass closure, and the 1/F enrichment — proved to machine precision by the pill above, and proved falsifiable by a shipped mutation harness that plants five bugs and checks each one trips.
The Settling Melt — the third live hall of The Deep Hearth, down inside the chamber the Melting Floor opens onto and the conduit draws from. Upstairs you make the melt; here you watch it come apart, and carry the record out in your hand. The cutaway backdrop and depth ribbon are the wing's shared section.mjs; the ordering, the enrichment and the core you pull are read directly from the self-tested core.mjs. Tap either pill (top-right) to re-run the proof or re-fire the payoff.
